lines.text: Enter Orlando and Adam.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: As I remember, Adam, it was upon this fashion bequeathed me by will but

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: poor a thousand crowns, and, as thou sayst, charged my brother, on his

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: blessing, to breed me well; and there begins my sadness. My brother

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Jaques he keeps at school, and report speaks goldenly of his profit.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: For my part, he keeps me rustically at home, or, to speak more

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: properly, stays me here at home unkept; for call you that keeping, for

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: a gentleman of my birth, that differs not from the stalling of an ox?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: His horses are bred better, for, besides that they are fair with their

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: feeding, they are taught their manage and to that end riders dearly

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: hired; but I, his brother, gain nothing under him but growth, for the

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: which his animals on his dunghills are as much bound to him as I.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Besides this nothing that he so plentifully gives me, the something

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: that nature gave me his countenance seems to take from me. He lets me

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: feed with his hinds, bars me the place of a brother, and as much as in

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: him lies, mines my gentility with my education. This is it, Adam, that

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: grieves me, and the spirit of my father, which I think is within me,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: begins to mutiny against this servitude. I will no longer endure it,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: though yet I know no wise remedy how to avoid it.
Enter Oliver.

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: Yonder comes my master, your brother.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Go apart, Adam, and thou shalt hear how he will shake me up.
[_Adam retires._]

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Now, sir, what make you here?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Nothing. I am not taught to make anything.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: What mar you then, sir?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Marry, sir, I am helping you to mar that which God made, a poor

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: unworthy brother of yours, with idleness.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Marry, sir, be better employed, and be naught awhile.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Shall I keep your hogs, and eat husks with them? What prodigal portion

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: have I spent that I should come to such penury?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Know you where you are, sir?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: O, sir, very well: here in your orchard.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Know you before whom, sir?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Ay, better than him I am before knows me. I know you are my eldest

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: brother, and in the gentle condition of blood you should so know me.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: The courtesy of nations allows you my better in that you are the

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: first-born, but the same tradition takes not away my blood, were there

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: twenty brothers betwixt us. I have as much of my father in me as you,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: albeit I confess your coming before me is nearer to his reverence.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: What, boy!

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Come, come, elder brother, you are too young in this.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Wilt thou lay hands on me, villain?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I am no villain. I am the youngest son of Sir Rowland de Boys; he was

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: my father, and he is thrice a villain that says such a father begot

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: villains. Wert thou not my brother, I would not take this hand from thy

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: throat till this other had pulled out thy tongue for saying so. Thou

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: has railed on thyself.
[_Coming forward_.]

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: Sweet masters, be patient. For your father’s

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: remembrance, be at accord.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Let me go, I say.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I will not till I please. You shall hear me. My father charged you in

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: his will to give me good education. You have trained me like a peasant,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: obscuring and hiding from me all gentleman-like qualities. The spirit

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: of my father grows strong in me, and I will no longer endure it.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Therefore allow me such exercises as may become a gentleman, or give me

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: the poor allottery my father left me by testament; with that I will go

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: buy my fortunes.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And what wilt thou do? Beg when that is spent? Well, sir, get you in. I

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: will not long be troubled with you. You shall have some part of your

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: will. I pray you leave me.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I no further offend you than becomes me for my good.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Get you with him, you old dog.

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: Is “old dog” my reward? Most true, I have lost my teeth in your

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: service. God be with my old master. He would not have spoke such a

lines.speaker: ADAM
lines.text: word.
[_Exeunt Orlando and Adam._]

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Is it even so? Begin you to grow upon me? I will physic your rankness,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: and yet give no thousand crowns neither. Holla, Dennis!
Enter Dennis.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: DENNIS

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Calls your worship?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Was not Charles, the Duke’s wrestler, here to speak with me?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: DENNIS

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: So please you, he is here at the door and importunes access to you.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Call him in.
[_Exit Dennis._]

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: ’Twill be a good way, and tomorrow the wrestling is.
Enter Charles.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Good morrow to your worship.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Good Monsieur Charles. What’s the new news at the new court?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: There’s no news at the court, sir, but the old news. That is, the old

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Duke is banished by his younger brother the new Duke, and three or four

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: loving lords have put themselves into voluntary exile with him, whose

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: lands and revenues enrich the new Duke; therefore he gives them good

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: leave to wander.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Can you tell if Rosalind, the Duke’s daughter, be banished with her

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: father?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: O, no; for the Duke’s daughter, her cousin, so loves her, being ever

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: from their cradles bred together, that she would have followed her

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: exile or have died to stay behind her. She is at the court and no less

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: beloved of her uncle than his own daughter, and never two ladies loved

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: as they do.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Where will the old Duke live?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: They say he is already in the Forest of Arden, and a many merry men

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: with him; and there they live like the old Robin Hood of England. They

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: say many young gentlemen flock to him every day and fleet the time

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: carelessly, as they did in the golden world.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: What, you wrestle tomorrow before the new Duke?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Marry, do I, sir, and I came to acquaint you with a matter. I am given,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: sir, secretly to understand that your younger brother Orlando hath a

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: disposition to come in disguised against me to try a fall. Tomorrow,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: sir, I wrestle for my credit, and he that escapes me without some

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: broken limb shall acquit him well. Your brother is but young and

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: tender, and for your love I would be loath to foil him, as I must for

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: my own honour if he come in. Therefore, out of my love to you, I came

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: hither to acquaint you withal, that either you might stay him from his

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: intendment, or brook such disgrace well as he shall run into, in that

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: it is a thing of his own search and altogether against my will.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Charles, I thank thee for thy love to me, which thou shalt find I will

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: most kindly requite. I had myself notice of my brother’s purpose

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: herein, and have by underhand means laboured to dissuade him from it;

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: but he is resolute. I’ll tell thee, Charles, it is the stubbornest

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: young fellow of France, full of ambition, an envious emulator of every

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: man’s good parts, a secret and villainous contriver against me his

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: natural brother. Therefore use thy discretion. I had as lief thou didst

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: break his neck as his finger. And thou wert best look to’t; for if thou

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: dost him any slight disgrace, or if he do not mightily grace himself on

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: thee, he will practise against thee by poison, entrap thee by some

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: treacherous device, and never leave thee till he hath ta’en thy life by

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: some indirect means or other. For I assure thee (and almost with tears

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: I speak it) there is not one so young and so villainous this day

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: living. I speak but brotherly of him, but should I anatomize him to

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: thee as he is, I must blush and weep, and thou must look pale and

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: wonder.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: I am heartily glad I came hither to you. If he come tomorrow I’ll give

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: him his payment. If ever he go alone again I’ll never wrestle for prize

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: more. And so, God keep your worship.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Farewell, good Charles. Now will I stir this gamester. I hope I shall

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: see an end of him; for my soul—yet I know not why—hates nothing more

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: than he. Yet he’s gentle, never schooled and yet learned, full of noble

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: device, of all sorts enchantingly beloved, and indeed so much in the

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: heart of the world, and especially of my own people, who best know him,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: that I am altogether misprized. But it shall not be so long; this

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: wrestler shall clear all. Nothing remains but that I kindle the boy

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: thither, which now I’ll go about.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A Lawn before the Duke’s Palace

lines.text: Enter Rosalind and Celia.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I pray thee, Rosalind, sweet my coz, be merry.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Dear Celia, I show more mirth than I am mistress of, and would you yet

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I were merrier? Unless you could teach me to forget a banished father,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: you must not learn me how to remember any extraordinary pleasure.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Herein I see thou lov’st me not with the full weight that I love thee.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: If my uncle, thy banished father, had banished thy uncle, the Duke my

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: father, so thou hadst been still with me, I could have taught my love

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: to take thy father for mine. So wouldst thou, if the truth of thy love

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: to me were so righteously tempered as mine is to thee.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Well, I will forget the condition of my estate to rejoice in yours.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: You know my father hath no child but I, nor none is like to have; and

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: truly, when he dies thou shalt be his heir, for what he hath taken away

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: from thy father perforce, I will render thee again in affection. By

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: mine honour I will! And when I break that oath, let me turn monster.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Therefore, my sweet Rose, my dear Rose, be merry.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: From henceforth I will, coz, and devise sports. Let me see—what think

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: you of falling in love?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Marry, I prithee do, to make sport withal; but love no man in good

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: earnest, nor no further in sport neither than with safety of a pure

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: blush thou mayst in honour come off again.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: What shall be our sport, then?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Let us sit and mock the good housewife Fortune from her wheel, that her

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: gifts may henceforth be bestowed equally.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I would we could do so, for her benefits are mightily misplaced, and

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: the bountiful blind woman doth most mistake in her gifts to women.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: ’Tis true, for those that she makes fair she scarce makes honest, and

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: those that she makes honest she makes very ill-favouredly.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, now thou goest from Fortune’s office to Nature’s. Fortune reigns

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: in gifts of the world, not in the lineaments of Nature.
Enter Touchstone.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: No? When Nature hath made a fair creature, may she not by Fortune fall

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: into the fire? Though Nature hath given us wit to flout at Fortune,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: hath not Fortune sent in this fool to cut off the argument?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Indeed, there is Fortune too hard for Nature, when Fortune makes

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nature’s natural the cutter-off of Nature’s wit.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Peradventure this is not Fortune’s work neither, but Nature’s, who

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: perceiveth our natural wits too dull to reason of such goddesses, and

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: hath sent this natural for our whetstone; for always the dullness of

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: the fool is the whetstone of the wits.—How now, wit, whither wander

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: you?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Mistress, you must come away to your father.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Were you made the messenger?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: No, by mine honour, but I was bid to come for you.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Where learned you that oath, fool?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Of a certain knight that swore by his honour they were good pancakes,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: and swore by his honour the mustard was naught. Now, I’ll stand to it,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: the pancakes were naught and the mustard was good, and yet was not the

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: knight forsworn.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: How prove you that in the great heap of your knowledge?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, marry, now unmuzzle your wisdom.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Stand you both forth now: stroke your chins, and swear by your beards

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: that I am a knave.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: By our beards, if we had them, thou art.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: By my knavery, if I had it, then I were. But if you swear by that that

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: is not, you are not forsworn. No more was this knight swearing by his

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: honour, for he never had any; or if he had, he had sworn it away before

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: ever he saw those pancackes or that mustard.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Prithee, who is’t that thou mean’st?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: One that old Frederick, your father, loves.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: My father’s love is enough to honour him. Enough! Speak no more of him.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: You’ll be whipped for taxation one of these days.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: The more pity that fools may not speak wisely what wise men do

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: foolishly.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: By my troth, thou sayest true. For since the little wit that fools have

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: was silenced, the little foolery that wise men have makes a great show.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Here comes Monsieur Le Beau.
Enter Le Beau.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With his mouth full of news.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Which he will put on us as pigeons feed their young.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then shall we be news-crammed.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: All the better; we shall be the more marketable.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: _Bonjour_, Monsieur Le Beau. What’s the news?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Fair princess, you have lost much good sport.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Sport! Of what colour?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: What colour, madam? How shall I answer you?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As wit and fortune will.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Or as the destinies decrees.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Well said. That was laid on with a trowel.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Nay, if I keep not my rank—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Thou losest thy old smell.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: You amaze me, ladies. I would have told you of good wrestling, which

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: you have lost the sight of.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Yet tell us the manner of the wrestling.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: I will tell you the beginning and, if it please your ladyships, you may

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: see the end, for the best is yet to do; and here, where you are, they

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: are coming to perform it.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Well, the beginning that is dead and buried.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: There comes an old man and his three sons—

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I could match this beginning with an old tale.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Three proper young men of excellent growth and presence.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With bills on their necks: “Be it known unto all men by these

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: presents.”

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: The eldest of the three wrestled with Charles, the Duke’s wrestler,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: which Charles in a moment threw him and broke three of his ribs, that

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: there is little hope of life in him. So he served the second, and so

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: the third. Yonder they lie, the poor old man their father making such

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: pitiful dole over them that all the beholders take his part with

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: weeping.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Alas!

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: But what is the sport, monsieur, that the ladies have lost?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Why, this that I speak of.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Thus men may grow wiser every day. It is the first time that ever I

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: heard breaking of ribs was sport for ladies.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Or I, I promise thee.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But is there any else longs to see this broken music in his sides? Is

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: there yet another dotes upon rib-breaking? Shall we see this wrestling,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: cousin?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: You must if you stay here, for here is the place appointed for the

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: wrestling, and they are ready to perform it.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Yonder, sure, they are coming. Let us now stay and see it.
Flourish. Enter Duke Frederick, Lords, Orlando, Charles and Attendants.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Come on. Since the youth will not be entreated, his own peril on his

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: forwardness.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Is yonder the man?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Even he, madam.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Alas, he is too young. Yet he looks successfully.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: How now, daughter and cousin? Are you crept hither to see the

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: wrestling?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, my liege, so please you give us leave.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: You will take little delight in it, I can tell you, there is such odds

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: in the man. In pity of the challenger’s youth I would fain dissuade

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: him, but he will not be entreated. Speak to him, ladies; see if you can

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: move him.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Call him hither, good Monsieur Le Beau.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Do so; I’ll not be by.
[_Duke Frederick steps aside._]

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Monsieur the challenger, the Princess calls for you.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I attend them with all respect and duty.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Young man, have you challenged Charles the wrestler?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: No, fair princess. He is the general challenger. I come but in as

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: others do, to try with him the strength of my youth.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Young gentleman, your spirits are too bold for your years. You have

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: seen cruel proof of this man’s strength. If you saw yourself with your

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: eyes or knew yourself with your judgement, the fear of your adventure

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: would counsel you to a more equal enterprise. We pray you for your own

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: sake to embrace your own safety and give over this attempt.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Do, young sir. Your reputation shall not therefore be misprized. We

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: will make it our suit to the Duke that the wrestling might not go

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: forward.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I beseech you, punish me not with your hard thoughts, wherein I confess

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: me much guilty to deny so fair and excellent ladies anything. But let

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: your fair eyes and gentle wishes go with me to my trial, wherein if I

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: be foiled there is but one shamed that was never gracious; if killed,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: but one dead that is willing to be so. I shall do my friends no wrong,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: for I have none to lament me; the world no injury, for in it I have

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: nothing. Only in the world I fill up a place, which may be better

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: supplied when I have made it empty.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: The little strength that I have, I would it were with you.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And mine to eke out hers.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Fare you well. Pray heaven I be deceived in you.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Your heart’s desires be with you.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Come, where is this young gallant that is so desirous to lie with his

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: mother earth?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Ready, sir; but his will hath in it a more modest working.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: You shall try but one fall.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: No, I warrant your grace you shall not entreat him to a second, that

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: have so mightily persuaded him from a first.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: You mean to mock me after; you should not have mocked me before. But

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: come your ways.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Now, Hercules be thy speed, young man!

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I would I were invisible, to catch the strong fellow by the leg.
[_Orlando and Charles wrestle._]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O excellent young man!

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: If I had a thunderbolt in mine eye, I can tell who should down.
[_Charles is thrown. Shout._]

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: No more, no more.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Yes, I beseech your grace. I am not yet well breathed.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: How dost thou, Charles?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: He cannot speak, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Bear him away.
[_Charles is carried off by Attendants._]

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: What is thy name, young man?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Orlando, my liege, the youngest son of Sir Rowland de Boys.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: I would thou hadst been son to some man else.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: The world esteemed thy father honourable,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: But I did find him still mine enemy.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Thou shouldst have better pleased me with this deed

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Hadst thou descended from another house.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: But fare thee well, thou art a gallant youth.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: I would thou hadst told me of another father.
[_Exeunt Duke Frederick, Le Beau and Lords._]

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Were I my father, coz, would I do this?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I am more proud to be Sir Rowland’s son,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: His youngest son, and would not change that calling

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: To be adopted heir to Frederick.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: My father loved Sir Rowland as his soul,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And all the world was of my father’s mind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Had I before known this young man his son,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I should have given him tears unto entreaties

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ere he should thus have ventured.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Gentle cousin,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Let us go thank him and encourage him.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: My father’s rough and envious disposition

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Sticks me at heart.—Sir, you have well deserved.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: If you do keep your promises in love

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But justly, as you have exceeded promise,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Your mistress shall be happy.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Gentleman,
[_Giving him a chain from her neck_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Wear this for me—one out of suits with Fortune,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That could give more but that her hand lacks means.—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Shall we go, coz?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Ay.—Fare you well, fair gentleman.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Can I not say, I thank you? My better parts

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Are all thrown down, and that which here stands up

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Is but a quintain, a mere lifeless block.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: He calls us back. My pride fell with my fortunes.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll ask him what he would.—Did you call, sir?—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Sir, you have wrestled well and overthrown

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: More than your enemies.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Will you go, coz?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Have with you.—Fare you well.
[_Exeunt Rosalind and Celia._]

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: What passion hangs these weights upon my tongue?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I cannot speak to her, yet she urged conference.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: O poor Orlando, thou art overthrown.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Or Charles or something weaker masters thee.
Enter Le Beau.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Good sir, I do in friendship counsel you

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: To leave this place. Albeit you have deserved

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: High commendation, true applause, and love,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Yet such is now the Duke’s condition

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: That he misconsters all that you have done.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: The Duke is humorous; what he is indeed

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: More suits you to conceive than I to speak of.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I thank you, sir; and pray you tell me this:

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Which of the two was daughter of the Duke

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: That here was at the wrestling?

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Neither his daughter, if we judge by manners,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: But yet indeed the smaller is his daughter.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: The other is daughter to the banished Duke,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: And here detained by her usurping uncle

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: To keep his daughter company, whose loves

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Are dearer than the natural bond of sisters.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: But I can tell you that of late this Duke

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Hath ta’en displeasure ’gainst his gentle niece,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Grounded upon no other argument

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: But that the people praise her for her virtues

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: And pity her for her good father’s sake;

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: And, on my life, his malice ’gainst the lady

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Will suddenly break forth. Sir, fare you well.

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: Hereafter, in a better world than this,

lines.speaker: LE BEAU
lines.text: I shall desire more love and knowledge of you.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I rest much bounden to you; fare you well!
[_Exit Le Beau._]

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Thus must I from the smoke into the smother,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: From tyrant Duke unto a tyrant brother.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: But heavenly Rosalind!
[_Exit._]
Enter Celia and Rosalind.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Why, cousin, why, Rosalind! Cupid have mercy! Not a word?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Not one to throw at a dog.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: No, thy words are too precious to be cast away upon curs. Throw some of

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: them at me. Come, lame me with reasons.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then there were two cousins laid up, when the one should be lamed with

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: reasons and the other mad without any.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But is all this for your father?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No, some of it is for my child’s father. O, how full of briers is this

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: working-day world!

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: They are but burs, cousin, thrown upon thee in holiday foolery. If we

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: walk not in the trodden paths, our very petticoats will catch them.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I could shake them off my coat; these burs are in my heart.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Hem them away.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I would try, if I could cry “hem” and have him.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Come, come, wrestle with thy affections.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O, they take the part of a better wrestler than myself.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O, a good wish upon you! You will try in time, in despite of a fall.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But turning these jests out of service, let us talk in good earnest. Is

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: it possible on such a sudden you should fall into so strong a liking

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: with old Sir Rowland’s youngest son?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: The Duke my father loved his father dearly.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Doth it therefore ensue that you should love his son dearly? By this

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: kind of chase I should hate him, for my father hated his father dearly;

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: yet I hate not Orlando.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No, faith, hate him not, for my sake.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Why should I not? Doth he not deserve well?
Enter Duke Frederick with Lords.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Let me love him for that, and do you love him because I do.—Look, here

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: comes the Duke.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: With his eyes full of anger.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Mistress, dispatch you with your safest haste,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: And get you from our court.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Me, uncle?

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: You, cousin.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Within these ten days if that thou be’st found

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: So near our public court as twenty miles,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Thou diest for it.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I do beseech your Grace,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Let me the knowledge of my fault bear with me.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: If with myself I hold intelligence,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Or have acquaintance with mine own desires,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: If that I do not dream, or be not frantic—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As I do trust I am not—then, dear uncle,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Never so much as in a thought unborn

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Did I offend your Highness.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Thus do all traitors.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: If their purgation did consist in words,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: They are as innocent as grace itself.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Let it suffice thee that I trust thee not.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Yet your mistrust cannot make me a traitor.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Tell me whereon the likelihood depends.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Thou art thy father’s daughter, there’s enough.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: So was I when your highness took his dukedom;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: So was I when your highness banished him.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Treason is not inherited, my lord,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Or, if we did derive it from our friends,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: What’s that to me? My father was no traitor.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then, good my liege, mistake me not so much

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: To think my poverty is treacherous.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Dear sovereign, hear me speak.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Ay, Celia, we stayed her for your sake,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Else had she with her father ranged along.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I did not then entreat to have her stay;

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: It was your pleasure and your own remorse.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I was too young that time to value her,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But now I know her. If she be a traitor,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Why, so am I. We still have slept together,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Rose at an instant, learned, played, ate together,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And wheresoe’er we went, like Juno’s swans,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Still we went coupled and inseparable.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: She is too subtle for thee, and her smoothness,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Her very silence, and her patience

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Speak to the people, and they pity her.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Thou art a fool. She robs thee of thy name,

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: And thou wilt show more bright and seem more virtuous

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: When she is gone. Then open not thy lips.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Firm and irrevocable is my doom

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: Which I have passed upon her. She is banished.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Pronounce that sentence then on me, my liege.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I cannot live out of her company.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: You are a fool. You, niece, provide yourself.

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: If you outstay the time, upon mine honour

lines.speaker: DUKE FREDERICK
lines.text: And in the greatness of my word, you die.
[_Exeunt Duke Frederick and Lords._]

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O my poor Rosalind, whither wilt thou go?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Wilt thou change fathers? I will give thee mine.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I charge thee, be not thou more grieved than I am.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I have more cause.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Thou hast not, cousin.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Prithee be cheerful. Know’st thou not the Duke

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Hath banished me, his daughter?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That he hath not.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: No, hath not? Rosalind lacks then the love

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Which teacheth thee that thou and I am one.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Shall we be sundered? Shall we part, sweet girl?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: No, let my father seek another heir.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Therefore devise with me how we may fly,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Whither to go, and what to bear with us,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And do not seek to take your change upon you,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: To bear your griefs yourself and leave me out.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: For, by this heaven, now at our sorrows pale,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Say what thou canst, I’ll go along with thee.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, whither shall we go?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: To seek my uncle in the Forest of Arden.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Alas, what danger will it be to us,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Maids as we are, to travel forth so far?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Beauty provoketh thieves sooner than gold.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I’ll put myself in poor and mean attire,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And with a kind of umber smirch my face.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: The like do you; so shall we pass along

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And never stir assailants.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Were it not better,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Because that I am more than common tall,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That I did suit me all points like a man?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A gallant curtal-axe upon my thigh,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A boar-spear in my hand, and in my heart

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Lie there what hidden woman’s fear there will,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: We’ll have a swashing and a martial outside,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As many other mannish cowards have

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That do outface it with their semblances.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: What shall I call thee when thou art a man?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll have no worse a name than Jove’s own page,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And therefore look you call me Ganymede.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But what will you be called?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Something that hath a reference to my state:

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: No longer Celia, but Aliena.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But, cousin, what if we assayed to steal

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: The clownish fool out of your father’s court?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Would he not be a comfort to our travel?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: He’ll go along o’er the wide world with me.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Leave me alone to woo him. Let’s away,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And get our jewels and our wealth together,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Devise the fittest time and safest way

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: To hide us from pursuit that will be made

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: After my flight. Now go we in content

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: To liberty, and not to banishment.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Duke Senior, Amiens and two or three Lords, dressed as foresters.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Now, my co-mates and brothers in exile,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Hath not old custom made this life more sweet

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Than that of painted pomp? Are not these woods

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: More free from peril than the envious court?

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Here feel we not the penalty of Adam,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: The seasons’ difference, as the icy fang

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: And churlish chiding of the winter’s wind,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Which when it bites and blows upon my body

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Even till I shrink with cold, I smile and say:

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: “This is no flattery. These are counsellors

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: That feelingly persuade me what I am.”

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Sweet are the uses of adversity,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Which, like the toad, ugly and venomous,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Wears yet a precious jewel in his head;

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: And this our life, exempt from public haunt,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Finds tongues in trees, books in the running brooks,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Sermons in stones, and good in everything.

lines.speaker: AMIENS
lines.text: I would not change it. Happy is your grace,

lines.speaker: AMIENS
lines.text: That can translate the stubbornness of fortune

lines.speaker: AMIENS
lines.text: Into so quiet and so sweet a style.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Come, shall we go and kill us venison?

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: And yet it irks me the poor dappled fools,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Being native burghers of this desert city,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Should in their own confines with forked heads

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Have their round haunches gored.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Indeed, my lord,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The melancholy Jaques grieves at that,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: And in that kind swears you do more usurp

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Than doth your brother that hath banished you.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Today my lord of Amiens and myself

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Did steal behind him as he lay along

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Under an oak, whose antique root peeps out

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Upon the brook that brawls along this wood;

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: To the which place a poor sequestered stag,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: That from the hunter’s aim had ta’en a hurt,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Did come to languish; and indeed, my lord,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The wretched animal heaved forth such groans

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: That their discharge did stretch his leathern coat

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Almost to bursting, and the big round tears

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Coursed one another down his innocent nose

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: In piteous chase. And thus the hairy fool,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Much marked of the melancholy Jaques,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Stood on th’ extremest verge of the swift brook,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Augmenting it with tears.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: But what said Jaques?

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Did he not moralize this spectacle?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: O yes, into a thousand similes.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: First, for his weeping into the needless stream:

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: “Poor deer,” quoth he “thou mak’st a testament

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: As worldlings do, giving thy sum of more

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: To that which had too much.” Then, being there alone,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Left and abandoned of his velvet friends:

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: “’Tis right”; quoth he, “thus misery doth part

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The flux of company.” Anon a careless herd,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Full of the pasture, jumps along by him

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: And never stays to greet him. “Ay,” quoth Jaques,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: “Sweep on, you fat and greasy citizens!

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: ’Tis just the fashion. Wherefore do you look

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
