lines.text: Peace, you dull fool, I found them on a tree.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Truly, the tree yields bad fruit.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll graft it with you, and then I shall graft it with a medlar. Then

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: it will be the earliest fruit i’ th’ country, for you’ll be rotten ere

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: you be half ripe, and that’s the right virtue of the medlar.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: You have said, but whether wisely or no, let the forest judge.
Enter Celia as Aliena, reading a paper.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Peace, here comes my sister, reading. Stand aside.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: _Why should this a desert be?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: For it is unpeopled? No!

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Tongues I’ll hang on every tree

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: That shall civil sayings show.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Some, how brief the life of man

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Runs his erring pilgrimage,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: That the streching of a span

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Buckles in his sum of age;

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Some, of violated vows

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: ’Twixt the souls of friend and friend.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But upon the fairest boughs,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Or at every sentence’ end,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Will I “Rosalinda” write,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Teaching all that read to know

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: The quintessence of every sprite

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Heaven would in little show.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Therefore heaven nature charged

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: That one body should be filled

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: With all graces wide-enlarged.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Nature presently distilled

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Helen’s cheek, but not her heart,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Cleopatra’s majesty;

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Atalanta’s better part,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Sad Lucretia’s modesty.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Thus Rosalind of many parts

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: By heavenly synod was devised,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Of many faces, eyes, and hearts

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: To have the touches dearest prized.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Heaven would that she these gifts should have,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And I to live and die her slave._

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O most gentle Jupiter, what tedious homily of love have you wearied

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: your parishioners withal, and never cried “Have patience, good people!”

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: How now! Back, friends. Shepherd, go off a little. Go with him, sirrah.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Come, shepherd, let us make an honourable retreat, though not with bag

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: and baggage, yet with scrip and scrippage.
[_Exeunt Corin and Touchstone._]

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Didst thou hear these verses?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O yes, I heard them all, and more too, for some of them had in them

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: more feet than the verses would bear.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: That’s no matter. The feet might bear the verses.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, but the feet were lame and could not bear themselves without the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: verse, and therefore stood lamely in the verse.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But didst thou hear without wondering how thy name should be hanged and

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: carved upon these trees?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I was seven of the nine days out of the wonder before you came; for

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: look here what I found on a palm-tree. I was never so berhymed since

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Pythagoras’ time that I was an Irish rat, which I can hardly remember.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Trow you who hath done this?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Is it a man?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And a chain, that you once wore, about his neck. Change you colour?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I prithee, who?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O Lord, Lord, it is a hard matter for friends to meet; but mountains

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: may be removed with earthquakes and so encounter.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, but who is it?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Is it possible?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, I prithee now, with most petitionary vehemence, tell me who it is.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O wonderful, wonderful, most wonderful wonderful, and yet again

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: wonderful, and after that, out of all whooping!

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Good my complexion! Dost thou think, though I am caparisoned like a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: man, I have a doublet and hose in my disposition? One inch of delay

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: more is a South Sea of discovery. I prithee tell me who is it quickly,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and speak apace. I would thou couldst stammer, that thou mightst pour

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: this concealed man out of thy mouth, as wine comes out of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: narrow-mouthed bottle—either too much at once or none at all. I prithee

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: take the cork out of thy mouth that I may drink thy tidings.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: So you may put a man in your belly.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Is he of God’s making? What manner of man? Is his head worth a hat, or

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: his chin worth a beard?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Nay, he hath but a little beard.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, God will send more if the man will be thankful. Let me stay the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: growth of his beard, if thou delay me not the knowledge of his chin.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: It is young Orlando, that tripped up the wrestler’s heels and your

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: heart both in an instant.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, but the devil take mocking! Speak sad brow and true maid.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I’ faith, coz, ’tis he.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Orlando?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Orlando.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Alas the day, what shall I do with my doublet and hose? What did he

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: when thou saw’st him? What said he? How looked he? Wherein went he?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: What makes he here? Did he ask for me? Where remains he? How parted he

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: with thee? And when shalt thou see him again? Answer me in one word.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: You must borrow me Gargantua’s mouth first. ’Tis a word too great for

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: any mouth of this age’s size. To say ay and no to these particulars is

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: more than to answer in a catechism.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But doth he know that I am in this forest and in man’s apparel? Looks

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: he as freshly as he did the day he wrestled?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: It is as easy to count atomies as to resolve the propositions of a

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: lover. But take a taste of my finding him, and relish it with good

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: observance. I found him under a tree, like a dropped acorn.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: It may well be called Jove’s tree when it drops forth such fruit.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Give me audience, good madam.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Proceed.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: There lay he, stretched along like a wounded knight.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Though it be pity to see such a sight, it well becomes the ground.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Cry “holla!” to thy tongue, I prithee. It curvets unseasonably. He was

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: furnished like a hunter.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O, ominous! He comes to kill my heart.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I would sing my song without a burden. Thou bring’st me out of tune.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Do you not know I am a woman? When I think, I must speak. Sweet, say

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: on.
Enter Orlando and Jaques.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: You bring me out. Soft, comes he not here?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: ’Tis he! Slink by, and note him.
[_Rosalind and Celia step aside._]

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I thank you for your company but, good faith, I had as lief have been

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: myself alone.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And so had I, but yet, for fashion sake, I thank you too for your

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: society.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: God be wi’ you, let’s meet as little as we can.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I do desire we may be better strangers.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I pray you, mar no more trees with writing love songs in their barks.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I pray you, mar no more of my verses with reading them ill-favouredly.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Rosalind is your love’s name?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Yes, just.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I do not like her name.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: There was no thought of pleasing you when she was christened.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: What stature is she of?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Just as high as my heart.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: You are full of pretty answers. Have you not been acquainted with

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: goldsmiths’ wives, and conned them out of rings?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Not so; but I answer you right painted cloth, from whence you have

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: studied your questions.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: You have a nimble wit. I think ’twas made of Atalanta’s heels. Will you

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: sit down with me? And we two will rail against our mistress the world

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: and all our misery.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I will chide no breather in the world but myself, against whom I know

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: most faults.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: The worst fault you have is to be in love.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: ’Tis a fault I will not change for your best virtue. I am weary of you.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: By my troth, I was seeking for a fool when I found you.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: He is drowned in the brook. Look but in, and you shall see him.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: There I shall see mine own figure.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Which I take to be either a fool or a cipher.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I’ll tarry no longer with you. Farewell, good Signior Love.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I am glad of your departure. Adieu, good Monsieur Melancholy.
[_Exit Jaques.—Celia and Rosalind come forward._]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will speak to him like a saucy lackey, and under that habit play the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: knave with him.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Do you hear, forester?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Very well. What would you?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I pray you, what is’t o’clock?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: You should ask me what time o’ day. There’s no clock in the forest.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then there is no true lover in the forest, else sighing every minute

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and groaning every hour would detect the lazy foot of time as well as a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: clock.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And why not the swift foot of time? Had not that been as proper?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: By no means, sir. Time travels in divers paces with divers persons.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll tell you who time ambles withal, who time trots withal, who time

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: gallops withal, and who he stands still withal.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I prithee, who doth he trot withal?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Marry, he trots hard with a young maid between the contract of her

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: marriage and the day it is solemnized. If the interim be but a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: se’nnight, time’s pace is so hard that it seems the length of seven

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: year.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Who ambles time withal?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With a priest that lacks Latin and a rich man that hath not the gout;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: for the one sleeps easily because he cannot study, and the other lives

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: merrily because he feels no pain; the one lacking the burden of lean

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and wasteful learning, the other knowing no burden of heavy tedious

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: penury. These time ambles withal.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Who doth he gallop withal?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With a thief to the gallows; for though he go as softly as foot can

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: fall, he thinks himself too soon there.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Who stays it still withal?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With lawyers in the vacation; for they sleep between term and term, and

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: then they perceive not how time moves.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Where dwell you, pretty youth?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: With this shepherdess, my sister, here in the skirts of the forest,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: like fringe upon a petticoat.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Are you native of this place?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As the coney that you see dwell where she is kindled.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Your accent is something finer than you could purchase in so removed a

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: dwelling.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I have been told so of many. But indeed an old religious uncle of mine

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: taught me to speak, who was in his youth an inland man, one that knew

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: courtship too well, for there he fell in love. I have heard him read

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: many lectures against it, and I thank God I am not a woman, to be

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: touched with so many giddy offences as he hath generally taxed their

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: whole sex withal.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Can you remember any of the principal evils that he laid to the charge

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: of women?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: There were none principal. They were all like one another as halfpence

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: are, every one fault seeming monstrous till his fellow fault came to

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: match it.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I prithee recount some of them.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No. I will not cast away my physic but on those that are sick. There is

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: a man haunts the forest that abuses our young plants with carving

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: “Rosalind” on their barks; hangs odes upon hawthorns and elegies on

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: brambles; all, forsooth, deifying the name of Rosalind. If I could meet

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: that fancy-monger, I would give him some good counsel, for he seems to

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: have the quotidian of love upon him.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I am he that is so love-shaked. I pray you tell me your remedy.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: There is none of my uncle’s marks upon you. He taught me how to know a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: man in love, in which cage of rushes I am sure you are not prisoner.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: What were his marks?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A lean cheek, which you have not; a blue eye and sunken, which you have

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: not; an unquestionable spirit, which you have not; a beard neglected,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: which you have not—but I pardon you for that, for simply your having in

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: beard is a younger brother’s revenue. Then your hose should be

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: ungartered, your bonnet unbanded, your sleeve unbuttoned, your shoe

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: untied, and everything about you demonstrating a careless desolation.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But you are no such man. You are rather point-device in your

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: accoutrements, as loving yourself than seeming the lover of any other.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Fair youth, I would I could make thee believe I love.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Me believe it? You may as soon make her that you love believe it, which

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I warrant she is apter to do than to confess she does. That is one of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: the points in the which women still give the lie to their consciences.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But, in good sooth, are you he that hangs the verses on the trees,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: wherein Rosalind is so admired?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I swear to thee, youth, by the white hand of Rosalind, I am that he,

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: that unfortunate he.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But are you so much in love as your rhymes speak?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Neither rhyme nor reason can express how much.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Love is merely a madness, and, I tell you, deserves as well a dark

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: house and a whip as madmen do; and the reason why they are not so

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: punished and cured is that the lunacy is so ordinary that the whippers

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: are in love too. Yet I profess curing it by counsel.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Did you ever cure any so?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Yes, one, and in this manner. He was to imagine me his love, his

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: mistress, and I set him every day to woo me; at which time would I,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: being but a moonish youth, grieve, be effeminate, changeable, longing

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and liking, proud, fantastical, apish, shallow, inconstant, full of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: tears, full of smiles; for every passion something and for no passion

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: truly anything, as boys and women are for the most part cattle of this

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: colour; would now like him, now loathe him; then entertain him, then

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: forswear him; now weep for him, then spit at him; that I drave my

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: suitor from his mad humour of love to a living humour of madness, which

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: was to forswear the full stream of the world and to live in a nook

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: merely monastic. And thus I cured him, and this way will I take upon me

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to wash your liver as clean as a sound sheep’s heart, that there shall

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: not be one spot of love in ’t.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I would not be cured, youth.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I would cure you, if you would but call me Rosalind and come every day

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to my cote and woo me.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Now, by the faith of my love, I will. Tell me where it is.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Go with me to it, and I’ll show it you; and by the way you shall tell

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: me where in the forest you live. Will you go?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: With all my heart, good youth.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, you must call me Rosalind. Come, sister, will you go?
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Touchstone and Audrey; Jaques at a distance observing them.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Come apace, good Audrey. I will fetch up your goats, Audrey. And how,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Audrey? Am I the man yet? Doth my simple feature content you?

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Your features, Lord warrant us! What features?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I am here with thee and thy goats, as the most capricious poet, honest

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Ovid, was among the Goths.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: O knowledge ill-inhabited, worse than Jove in a thatched

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: house!

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: When a man’s verses cannot be understood, nor a man’s good wit seconded

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: with the forward child, understanding, it strikes a man more dead than

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: a great reckoning in a little room. Truly, I would the gods had made

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: thee poetical.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: I do not know what “poetical” is. Is it honest in deed and word? Is it

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: a true thing?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: No, truly; for the truest poetry is the most feigning, and lovers are

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: given to poetry, and what they swear in poetry may be said, as lovers,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: they do feign.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Do you wish, then, that the gods had made me poetical?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I do, truly, for thou swear’st to me thou art honest. Now if thou wert

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: a poet, I might have some hope thou didst feign.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Would you not have me honest?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: No, truly, unless thou wert hard-favoured; for honesty coupled to

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: beauty is to have honey a sauce to sugar.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: A material fool!

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Well, I am not fair, and therefore I pray the gods make me honest.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Truly, and to cast away honesty upon a foul slut were to put good meat

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: into an unclean dish.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: I am not a slut, though I thank the gods I am foul.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Well, praised be the gods for thy foulness; sluttishness may come

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: hereafter. But be it as it may be, I will marry thee. And to that end I

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: have been with Sir Oliver Martext, the vicar of the next village, who

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: hath promised to meet me in this place of the forest and to couple us.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I would fain see this meeting.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Well, the gods give us joy!

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Amen. A man may, if he were of a fearful heart, stagger in this

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: attempt, for here we have no temple but the wood, no assembly but

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: horn-beasts. But what though? Courage! As horns are odious, they are

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: necessary. It is said, “Many a man knows no end of his goods.” Right.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Many a man has good horns and knows no end of them. Well, that is the

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: dowry of his wife; ’tis none of his own getting. Horns? Even so. Poor

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: men alone? No, no, the noblest deer hath them as huge as the rascal. Is

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: the single man therefore blessed? No. As a walled town is more worthier

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: than a village, so is the forehead of a married man more honourable

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: than the bare brow of a bachelor. And by how much defence is better

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: than no skill, by so much is horn more precious than to want.
Enter Sir Oliver Martext.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Here comes Sir Oliver. Sir Oliver Martext, you are well met. Will you

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: dispatch us here under this tree, or shall we go with you to your

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: chapel?

lines.speaker: MARTEXT
lines.text: Is there none here to give the woman?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I will not take her on gift of any man.

lines.speaker: MARTEXT
lines.text: Truly, she must be given, or the marriage is not lawful.
[_Coming forward_.]

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Proceed, proceed. I’ll give her.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Good even, good Master What-ye-call’t, how do you, sir? You are very

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: well met. God ’ild you for your last company. I am very glad to see

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: you. Even a toy in hand here, sir. Nay, pray be covered.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Will you be married, motley?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: As the ox hath his bow, sir, the horse his curb, and the falcon her

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: bells, so man hath his desires; and as pigeons bill, so wedlock would

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: be nibbling.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: And will you, being a man of your breeding, be married under a bush

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: like a beggar? Get you to church, and have a good priest that can tell

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: you what marriage is. This fellow will but join you together as they

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: join wainscot; then one of you will prove a shrunk panel, and like

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: green timber, warp, warp.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I am not in the mind but I were better to be married of him

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: than of another, for he is not like to marry me well, and not being

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: well married, it will be a good excuse for me hereafter to leave my

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: wife.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Go thou with me, and let me counsel thee.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Come, sweet Audrey. We must be married, or we must live in bawdry.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Farewell, good Master Oliver. Not

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: _O sweet Oliver,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: O brave Oliver,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Leave me not behind thee._

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: But

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: _Wind away,—

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Begone, I say,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I will not to wedding with thee._
[_Exeunt Touchstone, Audrey and Jaques._]

lines.speaker: MARTEXT
lines.text: ’Tis no matter. Ne’er a fantastical knave of them all shall flout me

lines.speaker: MARTEXT
lines.text: out of my calling.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Another part of the Forest. Before a Cottage

lines.text: Enter Rosalind and Celia.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Never talk to me, I will weep.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Do, I prithee, but yet have the grace to consider that tears do not

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: become a man.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But have I not cause to weep?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: As good cause as one would desire; therefore weep.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: His very hair is of the dissembling colour.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Something browner than Judas’s. Marry, his kisses are Judas’s own

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: children.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ faith, his hair is of a good colour.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: An excellent colour. Your chestnut was ever the only colour.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And his kissing is as full of sanctity as the touch of holy bread.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: He hath bought a pair of cast lips of Diana. A nun of winter’s

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: sisterhood kisses not more religiously; the very ice of chastity is in

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: them.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But why did he swear he would come this morning, and comes not?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Nay, certainly, there is no truth in him.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Do you think so?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Yes. I think he is not a pick-purse nor a horse-stealer, but for his

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: verity in love, I do think him as concave as a covered goblet or a

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: worm-eaten nut.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Not true in love?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Yes, when he is in, but I think he is not in.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: You have heard him swear downright he was.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: “Was” is not “is”. Besides, the oath of a lover is no stronger than the

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: word of a tapster. They are both the confirmer of false reckonings. He

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: attends here in the forest on the Duke your father.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I met the Duke yesterday, and had much question with him. He asked me

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: of what parentage I was. I told him, of as good as he, so he laughed

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and let me go. But what talk we of fathers when there is such a man as

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Orlando?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O, that’s a brave man! He writes brave verses, speaks brave words,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: swears brave oaths, and breaks them bravely, quite traverse, athwart

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: the heart of his lover, as a puny tilter, that spurs his horse but on

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: one side, breaks his staff like a noble goose. But all’s brave that

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: youth mounts and folly guides. Who comes here?
Enter Corin.

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Mistress and master, you have oft enquired

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: After the shepherd that complained of love,

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Who you saw sitting by me on the turf,

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Praising the proud disdainful shepherdess

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: That was his mistress.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Well, and what of him?

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: If you will see a pageant truly played

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Between the pale complexion of true love

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: And the red glow of scorn and proud disdain,

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Go hence a little, and I shall conduct you,

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: If you will mark it.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O, come, let us remove.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: The sight of lovers feedeth those in love.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Bring us to this sight, and you shall say

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll prove a busy actor in their play.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Silvius and Phoebe.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Sweet Phoebe, do not scorn me, do not, Phoebe.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Say that you love me not, but say not so

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: In bitterness. The common executioner,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Whose heart th’ accustomed sight of death makes hard,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Falls not the axe upon the humbled neck

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: But first begs pardon. Will you sterner be

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Than he that dies and lives by bloody drops?
Enter Rosalind, Celia and Corin, at a distance.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I would not be thy executioner;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I fly thee, for I would not injure thee.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Thou tell’st me there is murder in mine eye.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: ’Tis pretty, sure, and very probable

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: That eyes, that are the frail’st and softest things,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Who shut their coward gates on atomies,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Should be called tyrants, butchers, murderers.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Now I do frown on thee with all my heart,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And if mine eyes can wound, now let them kill thee.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Now counterfeit to swoon; why, now fall down;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Or if thou canst not, O, for shame, for shame,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Lie not, to say mine eyes are murderers.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Now show the wound mine eye hath made in thee.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Scratch thee but with a pin, and there remains

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Some scar of it; lean upon a rush,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: The cicatrice and capable impressure

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Thy palm some moment keeps. But now mine eyes,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Which I have darted at thee, hurt thee not;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Nor I am sure there is not force in eyes

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: That can do hurt.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: O dear Phoebe,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: If ever—as that ever may be near—

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: You meet in some fresh cheek the power of fancy,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Then shall you know the wounds invisible

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: That love’s keen arrows make.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But till that time

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Come not thou near me. And when that time comes,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Afflict me with thy mocks, pity me not,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: As till that time I shall not pity thee.
[_Advancing_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And why, I pray you? Who might be your mother,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That you insult, exult, and all at once,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Over the wretched? What though you have no beauty—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As, by my faith, I see no more in you

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Than without candle may go dark to bed—

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Must you be therefore proud and pitiless?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, what means this? Why do you look on me?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I see no more in you than in the ordinary

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Of nature’s sale-work. ’Od’s my little life,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I think she means to tangle my eyes too!

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No, faith, proud mistress, hope not after it.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: ’Tis not your inky brows, your black silk hair,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Your bugle eyeballs, nor your cheek of cream,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That can entame my spirits to your worship.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: You foolish shepherd, wherefore do you follow her,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Like foggy south, puffing with wind and rain?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: You are a thousand times a properer man

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Than she a woman. ’Tis such fools as you

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That makes the world full of ill-favoured children.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: ’Tis not her glass but you that flatters her,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And out of you she sees herself more proper

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Than any of her lineaments can show her.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But, mistress, know yourself; down on your knees,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And thank heaven, fasting, for a good man’s love.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: For I must tell you friendly in your ear,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Sell when you can; you are not for all markets.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Cry the man mercy, love him, take his offer;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Foul is most foul, being foul to be a scoffer.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: So take her to thee, shepherd. Fare you well.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Sweet youth, I pray you chide a year together!

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I had rather hear you chide than this man woo.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: He’s fall’n in love with your foulness, and she’ll fall in love with my

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: anger. If it be so, as fast as she answers thee with frowning looks,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll sauce her with bitter words. Why look you so upon me?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: For no ill will I bear you.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I pray you do not fall in love with me,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: For I am falser than vows made in wine.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Besides, I like you not. If you will know my house,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: ’Tis at the tuft of olives here hard by.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Will you go, sister? Shepherd, ply her hard.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Come, sister. Shepherdess, look on him better,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And be not proud. Though all the world could see,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: None could be so abused in sight as he.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Come, to our flock.
[_Exeunt Rosalind, Celia and Corin._]

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Dead shepherd, now I find thy saw of might:

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: “Who ever loved that loved not at first sight?”

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Sweet Phoebe—

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Ha, what sayst thou, Silvius?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Sweet Phoebe, pity me.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Why, I am sorry for thee, gentle Silvius.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Wherever sorrow is, relief would be.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: If you do sorrow at my grief in love,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: By giving love your sorrow and my grief

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Were both extermined.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Thou hast my love. Is not that neighbourly?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: I would have you.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Why, that were covetousness.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Silvius, the time was that I hated thee;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And yet it is not that I bear thee love;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But since that thou canst talk of love so well,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Thy company, which erst was irksome to me,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I will endure, and I’ll employ thee too.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But do not look for further recompense

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Than thine own gladness that thou art employed.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: So holy and so perfect is my love,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: And I in such a poverty of grace,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: That I shall think it a most plenteous crop

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: To glean the broken ears after the man

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: That the main harvest reaps. Loose now and then

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: A scattered smile, and that I’ll live upon.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Know’st thou the youth that spoke to me erewhile?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Not very well, but I have met him oft,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: And he hath bought the cottage and the bounds

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: That the old carlot once was master of.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Think not I love him, though I ask for him.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: ’Tis but a peevish boy—yet he talks well.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But what care I for words? Yet words do well

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: When he that speaks them pleases those that hear.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: It is a pretty youth—not very pretty—

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But sure he’s proud, and yet his pride becomes him.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: He’ll make a proper man. The best thing in him

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Is his complexion; and faster than his tongue

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Did make offence, his eye did heal it up.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: He is not very tall, yet for his years he’s tall;

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: His leg is but so-so, and yet ’tis well.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: There was a pretty redness in his lip,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: A little riper and more lusty red

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Than that mixed in his cheek. ’Twas just the difference

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Betwixt the constant red and mingled damask.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: There be some women, Silvius, had they marked him

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: In parcels as I did, would have gone near

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: To fall in love with him; but for my part

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I love him not nor hate him not; and yet

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I have more cause to hate him than to love him.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: For what had he to do to chide at me?

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: He said mine eyes were black and my hair black,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And now I am remembered, scorned at me.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I marvel why I answered not again.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: But that’s all one: omittance is no quittance.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I’ll write to him a very taunting letter,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And thou shalt bear it. Wilt thou, Silvius?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Phoebe, with all my heart.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I’ll write it straight,

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: The matter’s in my head and in my heart.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: I will be bitter with him and passing short.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Go with me, Silvius.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Rosalind, Celia and Jaques.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I prithee, pretty youth, let me be better acquainted with thee.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: They say you are a melancholy fellow.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I am so; I do love it better than laughing.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Those that are in extremity of either are abominable fellows, and

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: betray themselves to every modern censure worse than drunkards.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Why, ’tis good to be sad and say nothing.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why then, ’tis good to be a post.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I have neither the scholar’s melancholy, which is emulation; nor the

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: musician’s, which is fantastical; nor the courtier’s, which is proud;

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: nor the soldier’s, which is ambitious; nor the lawyer’s, which is

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: politic; nor the lady’s, which is nice; nor the lover’s, which is all

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: these; but it is a melancholy of mine own, compounded of many simples,

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: extracted from many objects, and indeed the sundry contemplation of my

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: travels, in which my often rumination wraps me in a most humorous

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: sadness.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A traveller! By my faith, you have great reason to be sad. I fear you

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: have sold your own lands to see other men’s. Then to have seen much and

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to have nothing is to have rich eyes and poor hands.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Yes, I have gained my experience.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And your experience makes you sad. I had rather have a fool to make me

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: merry than experience to make me sad—and to travel for it too.
Enter Orlando.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Good day and happiness, dear Rosalind!

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Nay, then, God be wi’ you, an you talk in blank verse.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Farewell, Monsieur Traveller. Look you lisp and wear strange suits;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: disable all the benefits of your own country; be out of love with your

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: nativity, and almost chide God for making you that countenance you are,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: or I will scarce think you have swam in a gondola.
[_Exit Jaques._]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, how now, Orlando, where have you been all this while? You a lover!

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: An you serve me such another trick, never come in my sight more.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: My fair Rosalind, I come within an hour of my promise.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Break an hour’s promise in love? He that will divide a minute into a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: thousand parts, and break but a part of the thousand part of a minute

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: in the affairs of love, it may be said of him that Cupid hath clapped

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: him o’ the shoulder, but I’ll warrant him heart-whole.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Pardon me, dear Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, an you be so tardy, come no more in my sight. I had as lief be

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: wooed of a snail.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Of a snail?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, of a snail, for though he comes slowly, he carries his house on his

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: head—a better jointure, I think, than you make a woman. Besides, he

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: brings his destiny with him.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: What’s that?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, horns, which such as you are fain to be beholding to your wives

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: for. But he comes armed in his fortune and prevents the slander of his

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: wife.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Virtue is no horn-maker and my Rosalind is virtuous.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And I am your Rosalind.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: It pleases him to call you so, but he hath a Rosalind of a better leer

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: than you.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Come, woo me, woo me, for now I am in a holiday humour, and like enough

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to consent. What would you say to me now, an I were your very, very

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Rosalind?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I would kiss before I spoke.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, you were better speak first, and when you were gravelled for lack

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: of matter, you might take occasion to kiss. Very good orators, when

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: they are out, they will spit; and for lovers lacking—God warn

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: us—matter, the cleanliest shift is to kiss.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: How if the kiss be denied?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then she puts you to entreaty, and there begins new matter.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Who could be out, being before his beloved mistress?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Marry, that should you, if I were your mistress, or I should think my

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: honesty ranker than my wit.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: What, of my suit?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Not out of your apparel, and yet out of your suit. Am not I your

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Rosalind?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I take some joy to say you are because I would be talking of her.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Well, in her person, I say I will not have you.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Then, in mine own person, I die.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No, faith, die by attorney. The poor world is almost six thousand years

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: old, and in all this time there was not any man died in his own person,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: _videlicet_, in a love-cause. Troilus had his brains dashed out with a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Grecian club, yet he did what he could to die before, and he is one of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: the patterns of love. Leander, he would have lived many a fair year

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: though Hero had turned nun, if it had not been for a hot midsummer

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: night; for, good youth, he went but forth to wash him in the Hellespont

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and, being taken with the cramp, was drowned; and the foolish

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: chroniclers of that age found it was Hero of Sestos. But these are all

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: lies. Men have died from time to time and worms have eaten them, but

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: not for love.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I would not have my right Rosalind of this mind, for I protest her

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: frown might kill me.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: By this hand, it will not kill a fly. But come, now I will be your

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Rosalind in a more coming-on disposition, and ask me what you will, I

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: will grant it.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Then love me, Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Yes, faith, will I, Fridays and Saturdays and all.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And wilt thou have me?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, and twenty such.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: What sayest thou?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Are you not good?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I hope so.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why then, can one desire too much of a good thing?—Come, sister, you

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: shall be the priest and marry us.—Give me your hand, Orlando.—What do

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: you say, sister?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Pray thee, marry us.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I cannot say the words.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: You must begin “Will you, Orlando—”

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Go to.—Will you, Orlando, have to wife this Rosalind?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I will.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, but when?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Why now, as fast as she can marry us.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Then you must say “I take thee, Rosalind, for wife.”

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I take thee, Rosalind, for wife.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I might ask you for your commission. But I do take thee, Orlando, for

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: my husband. There’s a girl goes before the priest, and certainly a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: woman’s thought runs before her actions.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: So do all thoughts. They are winged.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Now tell me how long you would have her after you have possessed her.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: For ever and a day.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Say “a day” without the “ever.” No, no, Orlando, men are April when

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: they woo, December when they wed. Maids are May when they are maids,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: but the sky changes when they are wives. I will be more jealous of thee

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: than a Barbary cock-pigeon over his hen, more clamorous than a parrot

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: against rain, more new-fangled than an ape, more giddy in my desires

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: than a monkey. I will weep for nothing, like Diana in the fountain, and

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will do that when you are disposed to be merry. I will laugh like a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: hyena, and that when thou are inclined to sleep.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: But will my Rosalind do so?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: By my life, she will do as I do.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: O, but she is wise.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Or else she could not have the wit to do this. The wiser, the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: waywarder. Make the doors upon a woman’s wit, and it will out at the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: casement. Shut that, and ’twill out at the keyhole. Stop that, ’twill

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: fly with the smoke out at the chimney.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: A man that had a wife with such a wit, he might say, “Wit, whither

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: wilt?”

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nay, you might keep that check for it till you met your wife’s wit

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: going to your neighbour’s bed.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And what wit could wit have to excuse that?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Marry, to say she came to seek you there. You shall never take her

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: without her answer unless you take her without her tongue. O, that

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: woman that cannot make her fault her husband’s occasion, let her never

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: nurse her child herself, for she will breed it like a fool.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: For these two hours, Rosalind, I will leave thee.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Alas, dear love, I cannot lack thee two hours.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I must attend the Duke at dinner. By two o’clock I will be with thee

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: again.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Ay, go your ways, go your ways. I knew what you would prove. My friends

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: told me as much, and I thought no less. That flattering tongue of yours

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: won me. ’Tis but one cast away, and so, come death! Two o’clock is your

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: hour?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Ay, sweet Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: By my troth, and in good earnest, and so God mend me, and by all pretty

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: oaths that are not dangerous, if you break one jot of your promise or

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: come one minute behind your hour, I will think you the most pathetical

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: break-promise, and the most hollow lover, and the most unworthy of her

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: you call Rosalind that may be chosen out of the gross band of the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: unfaithful. Therefore beware my censure, and keep your promise.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: With no less religion than if thou wert indeed my Rosalind. So, adieu.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Well, Time is the old justice that examines all such offenders, and let

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: time try. Adieu.
[_Exit Orlando._]

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: You have simply misused our sex in your love-prate! We must have your

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: doublet and hose plucked over your head and show the world what the

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: bird hath done to her own nest.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O coz, coz, coz, my pretty little coz, that thou didst know how many

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: fathom deep I am in love! But it cannot be sounded; my affection hath

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: an unknown bottom, like the Bay of Portugal.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Or rather, bottomless, that as fast as you pour affection in, it runs

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: out.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: No, that same wicked bastard of Venus, that was begot of thought,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: conceived of spleen, and born of madness, that blind rascally boy that

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: abuses everyone’s eyes because his own are out, let him be judge how

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: deep I am in love. I’ll tell thee, Aliena, I cannot be out of the sight

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: of Orlando. I’ll go find a shadow and sigh till he come.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And I’ll sleep.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Jaques and Lords, like foresters.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Which is he that killed the deer?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Sir, it was I.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Let’s present him to the Duke, like a Roman conqueror, and it would do

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: well to set the deer’s horns upon his head for a branch of victory.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Have you no song, forester, for this purpose?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Yes, sir.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Sing it. ’Tis no matter how it be in tune, so it make noise enough.
[_Sings_.]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: What shall he have that killed the deer?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: His leather skin and horns to wear.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Then sing him home:
[_The rest shall bear this burden_.]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Take thou no scorn to wear the horn.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: It was a crest ere thou wast born.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Thy father’s father wore it

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: And thy father bore it.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: The horn, the horn, the lusty horn

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Is not a thing to laugh to scorn.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Rosalind and Celia.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: How say you now? Is it not past two o’clock? And here much Orlando.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I warrant you, with pure love and troubled brain he hath ta’en his bow

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: and arrows and is gone forth to sleep.
Enter Silvius.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Look who comes here.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: My errand is to you, fair youth.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: My gentle Phoebe did bid me give you this.
[_Giving a letter._]

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: I know not the contents, but, as I guess

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: By the stern brow and waspish action

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Which she did use as she was writing of it,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: It bears an angry tenor. Pardon me,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: I am but as a guiltless messenger.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Patience herself would startle at this letter

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And play the swaggerer. Bear this, bear all!

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: She says I am not fair, that I lack manners;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: She calls me proud, and that she could not love me,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Were man as rare as phoenix. ’Od’s my will,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Her love is not the hare that I do hunt.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why writes she so to me? Well, shepherd, well,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: This is a letter of your own device.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: No, I protest, I know not the contents.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Phoebe did write it.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Come, come, you are a fool,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And turned into the extremity of love.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I saw her hand. She has a leathern hand,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A freestone-coloured hand. I verily did think

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That her old gloves were on, but ’twas her hands.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: She has a huswife’s hand—but that’s no matter.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I say she never did invent this letter;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: This is a man’s invention, and his hand.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Sure, it is hers.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, ’tis a boisterous and a cruel style,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: A style for challengers. Why, she defies me,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Like Turk to Christian. Women’s gentle brain

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Could not drop forth such giant-rude invention,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Such Ethiop words, blacker in their effect

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Than in their countenance. Will you hear the letter?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: So please you, for I never heard it yet,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Yet heard too much of Phoebe’s cruelty.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: She Phoebes me. Mark how the tyrant writes.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: _Art thou god to shepherd turned,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That a maiden’s heart hath burned?_

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Can a woman rail thus?

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Call you this railing?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: _Why, thy godhead laid apart,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Warr’st thou with a woman’s heart?_

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Did you ever hear such railing?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: _Whiles the eye of man did woo me,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: That could do no vengeance to me._

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Meaning me a beast.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: _If the scorn of your bright eyne

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Have power to raise such love in mine,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Alack, in me what strange effect

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Would they work in mild aspect?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Whiles you chid me, I did love,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: How then might your prayers move?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: He that brings this love to thee

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Little knows this love in me;

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And by him seal up thy mind,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Whether that thy youth and kind

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Will the faithful offer take

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Of me, and all that I can make,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Or else by him my love deny,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And then I’ll study how to die._

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: Call you this chiding?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Alas, poor shepherd.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Do you pity him? No, he deserves no pity.—Wilt thou love such a woman?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: What, to make thee an instrument and play false strains upon thee? Not

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to be endured! Well, go your way to her, for I see love hath made thee

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: a tame snake, and say this to her: that if she love me, I charge her to

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: love thee; if she will not, I will never have her unless thou entreat

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: for her. If you be a true lover, hence, and not a word, for here comes

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: more company.
[_Exit Silvius._]
Enter Oliver.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Good morrow, fair ones. Pray you, if you know,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Where in the purlieus of this forest stands

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: A sheepcote fenced about with olive trees?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: West of this place, down in the neighbour bottom;

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: The rank of osiers, by the murmuring stream,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Left on your right hand, brings you to the place.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: But at this hour the house doth keep itself.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: There’s none within.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: If that an eye may profit by a tongue,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Then should I know you by description,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Such garments, and such years. “The boy is fair,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Of female favour, and bestows himself

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Like a ripe sister; the woman low,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And browner than her brother.” Are not you

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: The owner of the house I did inquire for?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: It is no boast, being asked, to say we are.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Orlando doth commend him to you both,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And to that youth he calls his Rosalind

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: He sends this bloody napkin. Are you he?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I am. What must we understand by this?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Some of my shame, if you will know of me

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: What man I am, and how, and why, and where

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: This handkerchief was stained.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: I pray you tell it.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: When last the young Orlando parted from you,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: He left a promise to return again

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Within an hour, and pacing through the forest,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Chewing the food of sweet and bitter fancy,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Lo, what befell. He threw his eye aside,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And mark what object did present itself.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Under an oak, whose boughs were mossed with age

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And high top bald with dry antiquity,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: A wretched ragged man, o’ergrown with hair,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Lay sleeping on his back; about his neck

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: A green and gilded snake had wreathed itself,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Who with her head, nimble in threats, approached

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: The opening of his mouth. But suddenly,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Seeing Orlando, it unlinked itself

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And with indented glides did slip away

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Into a bush; under which bush’s shade

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: A lioness, with udders all drawn dry,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Lay couching, head on ground, with catlike watch

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: When that the sleeping man should stir. For ’tis

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: The royal disposition of that beast

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: To prey on nothing that doth seem as dead.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: This seen, Orlando did approach the man

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And found it was his brother, his elder brother.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: O, I have heard him speak of that same brother,

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: And he did render him the most unnatural

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: That lived amongst men.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And well he might so do,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: For well I know he was unnatural.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But, to Orlando: did he leave him there,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Food to the sucked and hungry lioness?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Twice did he turn his back and purposed so;

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: But kindness, nobler ever than revenge,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And nature, stronger than his just occasion,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Made him give battle to the lioness,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Who quickly fell before him; in which hurtling

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: From miserable slumber I awaked.

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Are you his brother?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Was it you he rescued?

lines.speaker: CELIA
lines.text: Was’t you that did so oft contrive to kill him?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: ’Twas I; but ’tis not I. I do not shame

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: To tell you what I was, since my conversion

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: So sweetly tastes, being the thing I am.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: But, for the bloody napkin?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: By and by.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: When from the first to last betwixt us two

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Tears our recountments had most kindly bathed—

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: As how I came into that desert place—

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: In brief, he led me to the gentle Duke,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Who gave me fresh array and entertainment,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Committing me unto my brother’s love,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Who led me instantly unto his cave,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: There stripped himself, and here upon his arm

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: The lioness had torn some flesh away,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Which all this while had bled; and now he fainted,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And cried in fainting upon Rosalind.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Brief, I recovered him, bound up his wound,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And after some small space, being strong at heart,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: He sent me hither, stranger as I am,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: To tell this story, that you might excuse

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: His broken promise, and to give this napkin,

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Dyed in his blood, unto the shepherd youth

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: That he in sport doth call his Rosalind.
[_Rosalind faints._]

lines.speaker: CELIA

lines.text: There is more in it. Cousin—Ganymede!

lines.text: I pray you, will you take him by the arm?

lines.text: Be of good cheer, youth. You a man? You lack a man’s heart.

lines.text: I do so, I confess it. Ah, sirrah, a body would think this was well

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: counterfeited. I pray you tell your brother how well I counterfeited.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Heigh-ho.

lines.text: This was not counterfeit. There is too great testimony in your

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: complexion that it was a passion of earnest.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Counterfeit, I assure you.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Well then, take a good heart, and counterfeit to be a man.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: So I do. But, i’ faith, I should have been a woman by right.

lines.text: Come, you look paler and paler. Pray you draw homewards. Good sir, go

lines.speaker: CELIA

lines.text: That will I, for I must bear answer back

lines.text: How you excuse my brother, Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND

Enter Touchstone and Audrey.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: We shall find a time, Audrey; patience, gentle Audrey.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Faith, the priest was good enough, for all the old gentleman’s saying.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: A most wicked Sir Oliver, Audrey, a most vile Martext. But Audrey,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: there is a youth here in the forest lays claim to you.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
