Enter William.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Here comes the man you mean.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: It is meat and drink to me to see a clown. By my troth, we that have

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: good wits have much to answer for. We shall be flouting; we cannot

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: hold.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Good ev’n, Audrey.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: God ye good ev’n, William.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: And good ev’n to you, sir.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Good ev’n, gentle friend. Cover thy head, cover thy head. Nay, prithee,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: be covered. How old are you, friend?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Five-and-twenty, sir.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: A ripe age. Is thy name William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: William, sir.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: A fair name. Wast born i’ th’ forest here?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Ay, sir, I thank God.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: “Thank God.” A good answer. Art rich?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Faith, sir, so-so.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: “So-so” is good, very good, very excellent good. And yet it is not, it

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: is but so-so. Art thou wise?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Ay, sir, I have a pretty wit.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Why, thou sayst well. I do now remember a saying: “The fool doth think

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.” The heathen

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: philosopher, when he had a desire to eat a grape, would open his lips

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: when he put it into his mouth, meaning thereby that grapes were made to

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: eat and lips to open. You do love this maid?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: I do, sir.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Give me your hand. Art thou learned?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: No, sir.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Then learn this of me: to have is to have. For it is a figure in

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: rhetoric that drink, being poured out of cup into a glass, by filling

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: the one doth empty the other. For all your writers do consent that

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: _ipse_ is “he.” Now, you are not _ipse_, for I am he.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Which he, sir?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: He, sir, that must marry this woman. Therefore, you clown,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: abandon—which is in the vulgar, “leave”—the society—which in the

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: boorish is “company”—of this female—which in the common is “woman”;

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: which together is, abandon the society of this female, or, clown, thou

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: perishest; or, to thy better understanding, diest; or, to wit, I kill

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: thee, make thee away, translate thy life into death, thy liberty into

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: bondage. I will deal in poison with thee, or in bastinado, or in steel.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I will bandy with thee in faction; will o’errun thee with policy. I

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: will kill thee a hundred and fifty ways! Therefore tremble and depart.

lines.speaker: AUDREY
lines.text: Do, good William.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: God rest you merry, sir.
[_Exit._]
Enter Corin.

lines.speaker: CORIN
lines.text: Our master and mistress seek you. Come away, away.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: Trip, Audrey, trip, Audrey! I attend, I attend.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Orlando and Oliver.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Is’t possible that on so little acquaintance you should like her? That

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: but seeing, you should love her? And loving woo? And wooing, she should

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: grant? And will you persever to enjoy her?

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: Neither call the giddiness of it in question, the poverty of her, the

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: small acquaintance, my sudden wooing, nor her sudden consenting. But

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: say with me, I love Aliena; say with her that she loves me; consent

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: with both that we may enjoy each other. It shall be to your good, for

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: my father’s house and all the revenue that was old Sir Rowland’s will I

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: estate upon you, and here live and die a shepherd.
Enter Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: You have my consent. Let your wedding be tomorrow. Thither will I

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: invite the Duke and all’s contented followers. Go you and prepare

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Aliena; for, look you, here comes my Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: God save you, brother.

lines.speaker: OLIVER
lines.text: And you, fair sister.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O my dear Orlando, how it grieves me to see thee wear thy heart in a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: scarf!

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: It is my arm.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I thought thy heart had been wounded with the claws of a lion.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Wounded it is, but with the eyes of a lady.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Did your brother tell you how I counterfeited to swoon when he showed

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: me your handkercher?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Ay, and greater wonders than that.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: O, I know where you are. Nay, ’tis true. There was never anything so

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: sudden but the fight of two rams, and Caesar’s thrasonical brag of “I

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: came, saw and overcame.” For your brother and my sister no sooner met

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: but they looked; no sooner looked but they loved; no sooner loved but

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: they sighed; no sooner sighed but they asked one another the reason; no

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: sooner knew the reason but they sought the remedy; and in these degrees

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: have they made pair of stairs to marriage, which they will climb

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: incontinent, or else be incontinent before marriage. They are in the

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: very wrath of love, and they will together. Clubs cannot part them.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: They shall be married tomorrow, and I will bid the Duke to the nuptial.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: But O, how bitter a thing it is to look into happiness through another

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: man’s eyes! By so much the more shall I tomorrow be at the height of

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: heart-heaviness, by how much I shall think my brother happy in having

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: what he wishes for.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Why, then, tomorrow I cannot serve your turn for Rosalind?

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: I can live no longer by thinking.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will weary you then no longer with idle talking. Know of me then—for

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: now I speak to some purpose—that I know you are a gentleman of good

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: conceit. I speak not this that you should bear a good opinion of my

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: knowledge, insomuch I say I know you are. Neither do I labour for a

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: greater esteem than may in some little measure draw a belief from you,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to do yourself good, and not to grace me. Believe then, if you please,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: that I can do strange things. I have, since I was three year old,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: conversed with a magician, most profound in his art and yet not

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: damnable. If you do love Rosalind so near the heart as your gesture

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: cries it out, when your brother marries Aliena shall you marry her. I

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: know into what straits of fortune she is driven and it is not

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: impossible to me, if it appear not inconvenient to you, to set her

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: before your eyes tomorrow, human as she is, and without any danger.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Speak’st thou in sober meanings?

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: By my life, I do, which I tender dearly, though I say I am a magician.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Therefore put you in your best array, bid your friends; for if you will

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: be married tomorrow, you shall, and to Rosalind, if you will.

lines.text: Youth, you have done me much ungentleness

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: To show the letter that I writ to you.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I care not if I have; it is my study

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: To seem despiteful and ungentle to you.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: You are there followed by a faithful shepherd.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Look upon him, love him; he worships you.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Good shepherd, tell this youth what ’tis to love.

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: And so am I for Phoebe.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And I for Ganymede.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And I for Rosalind.

lines.text: And I for no woman.

lines.text: And so am I for Phoebe.

lines.text: And I for Rosalind.

lines.text: And I for no woman.

lines.text: It is to be all made of fantasy,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: All made of passion, and all made of wishes,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: All adoration, duty, and observance,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: All humbleness, all patience, and impatience,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: All purity, all trial, all observance,

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: And so am I for Phoebe.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: And so am I for Ganymede.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: And so am I for Rosalind.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: And so am I for no woman.
[_To Rosalind_.]

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: If this be so, why blame you me to love you?
[_To Phoebe_.]

lines.speaker: SILVIUS
lines.text: If this be so, why blame you me to love you?

lines.text: If this be so, why blame you me to love you?

lines.text: Why do you speak too, “Why blame you me to love you?”

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: To her that is not here, nor doth not hear.

lines.text: Pray you, no more of this, ’tis like the howling of Irish wolves

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: against the moon.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will help you if I can.
[_to Phoebe_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I would love you if I could.—Tomorrow meet me all

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: together.
[_to Phoebe_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will marry you, if ever I marry woman, and I’ll be

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: married tomorrow.
[_to Orlando_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will satisfy you if ever I satisfied man, and you

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: shall be married tomorrow.
[_to Silvius_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I will content you, if what pleases you contents you,

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: and you shall be married tomorrow.
[_to Orlando_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As you love Rosalind, meet.
[_to Silvius_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: As you love Phoebe, meet.—And as I love no woman, I’ll

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: meet. So fare you well. I have left you commands.

lines.text: I’ll not fail, if I live.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.speaker: ORLANDO
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.text: Upon a lie seven times removed—bear your body more seeming, Audrey—as

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: thus, sir. I did dislike the cut of a certain courtier’s beard. He sent

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: me word if I said his beard was not cut well, he was in the mind it

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: was. This is called the “retort courteous”. If I sent him word again it

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: was not well cut, he would send me word he cut it to please himself.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: This is called the “quip modest”. If again it was not well cut, he

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: disabled my judgement. This is called the “reply churlish”. If again it

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: was not well cut, he would answer I spake not true. This is called the

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: “reproof valiant”. If again it was not well cut, he would say I lie.

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: This is called the “countercheck quarrelsome”, and so, to the “lie

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: circumstantial”, and the “lie direct”.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: And how oft did you say his beard was not well cut?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: I durst go no further than the lie circumstantial, nor he durst not

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: give me the lie direct; and so we measured swords and parted.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Can you nominate in order now the degrees of the lie?

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: O sir, we quarrel in print, by the book, as you have books for good

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: manners. I will name you the degrees: the first, the retort courteous;

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: the second, the quip modest; the third, the reply churlish; the fourth,

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: the reproof valiant; the fifth, the countercheck quarrelsome; the

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: sixth, the lie with circumstance; the seventh, the lie direct. All

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: these you may avoid but the lie direct and you may avoid that too with

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: an “if”. I knew when seven justices could not take up a quarrel, but

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: when the parties were met themselves, one of them thought but of an

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: “if”, as, “if you said so, then I said so;” and they shook hands, and

lines.speaker: TOUCHSTONE
lines.text: swore brothers. Your “if” is the only peacemaker; much virtue in “if.”

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: Is not this a rare fellow, my lord? He’s as good at anything, and yet a

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: fool.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: He uses his folly like a stalking-horse, and under the presentation of

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: that he shoots his wit.

lines.text: Hymen from heaven brought her,

lines.text: Yea, brought her hither,

lines.text: That thou mightst join her hand with his,

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Whose heart within his bosom is.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: To you I give myself, for I am yours.

lines.text: If there be truth in sight, you are my daughter.

lines.text: If there be truth in sight, you are my Rosalind.

lines.speaker: PHOEBE
lines.text: If sight and shape be true,

lines.text: Why then, my love adieu.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll have no father, if you be not he.
[_To Orlando_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I’ll have no husband, if you be not he.
[_To Phoebe_.]

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: Nor ne’er wed woman, if you be not she.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Peace, ho! I bar confusion.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: ’Tis I must make conclusion

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Of these most strange events.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Here’s eight that must take hands

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: To join in Hymen’s bands,

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: If truth holds true contents.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: You and you no cross shall part.
[_To Celia and Oliver_.]

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: You and you are heart in heart.
[_To Phoebe_.]

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: You to his love must accord

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Or have a woman to your lord.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: You and you are sure together

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: As the winter to foul weather.

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Whiles a wedlock hymn we sing,

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: Feed yourselves with questioning,

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: That reason wonder may diminish

lines.speaker: HYMEN
lines.text: How thus we met, and these things finish.

lines.text: ’Tis Hymen peoples every town,

lines.text: Honour, high honour, and renown

lines.text: O my dear niece, welcome thou art to me

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR

[_To Silvius_.]

lines.text: Let me have audience for a word or two.

lines.text: I am the second son of old Sir Rowland,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: That bring these tidings to this fair assembly.

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: Duke Frederick, hearing how that every day

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: Men of great worth resorted to this forest,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: Addressed a mighty power, which were on foot

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: In his own conduct, purposely to take

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: His brother here and put him to the sword;

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: And to the skirts of this wild wood he came,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: Where, meeting with an old religious man,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: After some question with him, was converted

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: Both from his enterprise and from the world,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: His crown bequeathing to his banished brother,

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: And all their lands restored to them again

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS
lines.text: That were with him exiled. This to be true

lines.speaker: JAQUES DE BOYS

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Welcome, young man.

lines.text: Thou offer’st fairly to thy brother’s wedding:

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: To one his lands withheld, and to the other

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: A land itself at large, a potent dukedom.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: First, in this forest let us do those ends

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: That here were well begun and well begot;

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: And after, every of this happy number

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: That have endured shrewd days and nights with us

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Shall share the good of our returned fortune,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: According to the measure of their states.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Meantime, forget this new-fall’n dignity,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: And fall into our rustic revelry.

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Play, music! And you brides and bridegrooms all,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: With measure heaped in joy to th’ measures fall.

lines.text: Sir, by your patience. If I heard you rightly,

lines.speaker: JAQUES

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: You to a love that your true faith doth merit.

lines.speaker: JAQUES

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: I am for other than for dancing measures.

lines.text: Stay, Jaques, stay.

lines.speaker: JAQUES
lines.text: To see no pastime, I. What you would have

lines.speaker: JAQUES

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR
lines.text: Proceed, proceed! We will begin these rites,

lines.speaker: DUKE SENIOR

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: It is not the fashion to see the lady the epilogue, but it is no more

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: unhandsome than to see the lord the prologue. If it be true that good

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: wine needs no bush, ’tis true that a good play needs no epilogue. Yet

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to good wine they do use good bushes, and good plays prove the better

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: by the help of good epilogues. What a case am I in then, that am

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: neither a good epilogue nor cannot insinuate with you in the behalf of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: a good play! I am not furnished like a beggar; therefore to beg will

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: not become me. My way is to conjure you, and I’ll begin with the women.

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: I charge you, O women, for the love you bear to men, to like as much of

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: this play as please you. And I charge you, O men, for the love you bear

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: to women—as I perceive by your simpering, none of you hates them—that

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: between you and the women the play may please. If I were a woman, I

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: would kiss as many of you as had beards that pleased me, complexions

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: that liked me, and breaths that I defied not. And I am sure as many as

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: have good beards, or good faces, or sweet breaths will for my kind

lines.speaker: ROSALIND
lines.text: offer, when I make curtsy, bid me farewell.
[_Exit._]
